When a company raises venture money, a clock starts. Growth has to keep pace with the next round. That pressure tends to leak into the product: collect a bit more data, push a few more upsells, and consider a data deal that looks tempting in a bad quarter.

We don't have that clock.

Plausible is independent, self-funded and profitable. We're based in the EU. We don't sell customer data, and our business doesn't depend on it.

We're paid by our subscribers, over 21,000 of them. Not by selling what we learn about their visitors. That keeps our incentives simple: build analytics that site owners want to keep paying for.

If you're deciding where your website's traffic data should live, ask every vendor one question:

How do you make money?

The answer tells you most of what you need to know about what happens to your data.

None of that is automatically bad, but whoever pays decides what the tool is built to do with your visitors' visits.

So the honest check takes five minutes. Open the vendor's pricing page and its privacy policy side by side, then answer two questions. Who pays for this? And is my visitors' data part of what they get?

Here is our answer at Plausible. More than 21,000 site owners pay for it. We're self-funded, profitable and based in the EU, and we don't sell customer data. The script uses no cookies and collects no personal data, so there is no personal information about your visitors on our side for anyone to buy.

It also means Plausible isn't free. I'd rather you knew exactly what you're paying and who you're paying than wonder later.

posts.title: The analytics script you load on every pageview

emails.previewText: Page speed and a cookie banner.
emails.body:
Hi {{first_name|there}},

Most analytics setups quietly cost you two things.

1. Speed
Every script you add has to load. Plausible's script is 54 times smaller than Google Analytics, so measuring your traffic doesn't slow down the site you're measuring.

2. A cookie banner
Cookie-based analytics usually means asking visitors for consent. That's a banner people find annoying. It also leaves gaps in your numbers, because visitors who click 'reject' aren't counted. Plausible doesn't use cookies or collect personal data, so it doesn't need a cookie banner or a GDPR consent form.

One honest note: if other tools on your site set cookies, those tools may still need consent. Plausible removes analytics from that list.

If both of these matter to you, start a free trial and add the script to your site. You'll see your own traffic in Plausible soon after visitors start arriving, so you can compare it with what you use today.
